study_identification.author_journal_year: Yu et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2024
study_identification.title: Behavioral and brain morphological changes before and after hemispherotomy

study_characteristics.study_objective: To systematically investigate changes in gray matter volume (GMV) before and after hemispherotomy surgery in pediatric epilepsy patients, and to analyze their relationships with behavioral recovery, as well as to examine whether preoperative GMV features can predict postoperative behavioral outcomes.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ABIDE-I; ABIDE-II; BCP; CPMD; CBD; CCNP; HBN; HCPD; IBIS; PeriCBD; PING; Pixar; and other studies)

hc_age.answer: mean and sd not reported; age range 0.3-13.0 years

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: SPM12; Serial Longitudinal Registration toolbox; Voxel-based morphometry (VBM); symmetric T1 template in MNI space; 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel smoothing

quality_checking_detail.answer: Visual inspection for quality control at each processing step. Poor quality images or images with poor GM/WM contrast (especially in younger babies) were excluded. Among 2343 initially included healthy children aged 0.3-13.0 years, 228 (9.7%) were excluded due to poor image quality or image processing failure, resulting in 2115 children for analysis. For patients, 17 out of 74 (23.0%) were excluded due to poor quality of either pre- or postoperative MRI images (e.g., severe head motion, bad intensity contrast, abnormalities and severe distortion of the unaffected regions).

predictor_effects.answer: Age and Sex were included as covariates in the Gaussian process regression model. The specific fixed/random effect specification is not explicitly stated, but standard GPR treats covariates as fixed effects within the kernel function.

clinical_dataset.answer: Peking University First Hospital pediatric epilepsy patients undergoing peri-insular hemispherotomy

diseases_studied.answer: Refractory epilepsy (pediatric patients with diffuse unihemispheric lesions)

clinical_groups_age.answer: Left hemispherotomy: mean 3.5±2.5 years (range 0.7-10.6); Right hemispherotomy: mean 4.6±2.5 years (range 1.1-11.0)

clinical_groups_sex.answer: Left hemispherotomy: F 13 (44.8%), M 16 (55.2%); Right hemispherotomy: F 12 (42.9%), M 16 (57.1%)

deviation_metric.answer: Z-score representing individual deviation from age- and sex-matched normative GMV; positive Z indicates GM expansion relative to norm, negative Z indicates GM shrinkage/underdevelopment relative to norm

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear mixed-effects model (LMEM) with 'MRI to surgery' time and other covariates (epilepsy onset, age at surgery, sex, etiology) as fixed effects and 'individual identities' as random effects, allowing intercept and slope to vary across individuals. Voxelwise LMEM within unaffected GM regions to evaluate pre-post GMV changes (multiple comparison correction using random field theory, uncorrected p<0.001, cluster-corrected p<0.05/2 for two patient groups). Pearson correlation between GMV change and behavioral score change for identified clusters. Machine learning regression (SVR, LASSO, ridge regression) with nested leave-one-out cross-validation to predict postoperative behavioral scores from preoperative GMV features; permutation testing (1000 iterations) for significance; Wilcoxon signed-rank test to compare prediction performance between left and right groups; permutation procedure for feature weight assessment with FDR correction (p<0.05) to identify significantly contributing features.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Both left and right hemispherotomy patients showed widespread GMV increases in contralateral cerebrum and ipsilateral cerebellum, but GMV decreases in contralateral cerebellum; GMV decrease in contralateral cerebellum significantly correlated with behavioral improvement in right (r=-0.64, p=0.007) but not left hemispherotomy patients; preoperative GMV features significantly predicted postoperative behavioral scores in both groups (left: r=0.52, p=0.006; right: r=0.48, p=0.021).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using normative modeling to control for developmental effects, the study revealed consistent neuroplastic changes in 57 pediatric hemispherotomy patients (29 left, 28 right). Most patients showed overall GM underdevelopment preoperatively (79% of left and 71% of right patients had >80% of voxels with negative Z-scores). Post-surgery, both groups exhibited: (1) significantly increased age-adjusted GMV in the contralateral cerebrum (left: t=6.92, p<0.001; right: t=7.44, p<0.001; 100% and 96.4% of patients showed increases), indicating greater GM growth than age-matched healthy children; (2) increased GMV in ipsilateral cerebellum (left: t=6.95, p<0.001; right: t=8.53, p<0.001; 100% of patients in both groups); (3) decreased GMV in contralateral cerebellum (left: t=-8.32, p<0.001; right: t=-7.73, p<0.001; 82.8% and 96.4% showed decreases). Additionally, left hemispherotomy patients uniquely showed decreased GMV in contralateral cingulate gyrus (t=-5.23, p<0.001; 79.3% showed decreases). Crucially, contralateral cerebellar GMV decrease significantly correlated with behavioral improvement in right (r=-0.64, p=0.007) but not left (r=-0.10, p=0.73) hemispherotomy patients. Machine learning models using preoperative GMV significantly predicted postoperative behavioral scores (ridge regression: left r=0.52 NRMSE=0.20 p=0.006, right r=0.48 NRMSE=0.25 p=0.021; better performance in left group p=0.002). Significant predictive features for left patients: bilateral cerebellum and contralateral occipital lobe; for right patients: bilateral cerebellum and contralateral temporal lobe. Both groups showed significant behavioral improvement post-surgery (left: t=2.10, p=0.04; right: t=3.97, p<0.001).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Small absolute sample size (n=57 total; 29 left, 28 right) despite being relatively large for hemispherotomy studies; limited generalizability and confidence in machine learning prediction validity due to small training set size; requires validation in larger independent cohorts from different hospitals/sources. Behavioral assessment available for only subset of patients (19 left and 19 right for pre-post comparison). Lack of explicit multi-site harmonization despite using normative data from 11 datasets with different scanners (1.5T and 3T) and protocols. Difficulty distinguishing GM/WM boundaries in younger babies, though poor quality images were excluded. Mechanisms underlying observed GMV changes cannot be definitively separated (neurodevelopment vs. neurodegeneration vs. neuroplasticity). Cross-sectional nature of normative reference data (single timepoint per child) may not fully capture individual developmental trajectories. Unclear whether observed patterns generalize to other hemispherotomy surgical techniques beyond peri-insular approach.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study highlights important clinical potential of preoperative structural MRI for predicting postoperative behavioral outcomes in hemispherotomy patients. Unlike previous univariate predictors (contralateral MRI abnormalities, brainstem/corticospinal tract asymmetries, sensorimotor fMRI), this multivariate machine learning framework using whole-brain GMV patterns shows robust prediction performance and excellent clinical applicability as features are easily derived from routine structural MRI. The normative modeling approach successfully controlled for dramatic developmental effects in pediatric populations, enabling valid longitudinal comparisons. Findings suggest differential neuroplastic mechanisms between left and right hemispherotomy (e.g., unique cingulate gyrus changes in left; cerebellum-behavior correlation only in right), indicating they should be evaluated separately. Results support a positive neuroplastic role of contralateral cerebellar atrophy in behavioral recovery following right hemispherotomy. The study provides novel insight into GM morphological changes accompanying behavioral recovery, complementing previous studies focused on functional activation and white matter integrity. Widespread GM growth in contralateral cerebrum may relate to loss of interhemispheric inhibition following disconnection. Future work should validate findings in larger independent cohorts and investigate underlying mechanisms for hemisphere-dependent phenomena.
